heroHeadline: 11 Days to Kickoff — PSG Win UCL Final (Hakimi Champion); Argentina Confirm Messi; Opening Ceremony Lineups: Katy Perry & Alanis Morissette; Iran Has Zero US Visas
heroSubtitle: Paris Saint-Germain retained the UEFA Champions League title on May 30, defeating Arsenal 1-1 (4-3 on penalties) in Budapest — PSG became the first back-to-back champions in the modern era. Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi lifted the trophy just 12 days before Morocco open the World Cup vs Scotland (June 20, MetLife). Brazil's Gabriel Magalhães, who missed the decisive penalty, remains in Ancelotti's 26-man squad. Argentina officially confirmed their 26-man World Cup roster on May 30 with Lionel Messi included despite a May 24 hamstring scare — coach Scaloni called the injury 'not that bad.' Messi equals Cristiano Ronaldo's record of six World Cup appearances; Dybala, Garnacho, and Mastantuono were cut. FIFA revealed all three opening ceremony lineups on May 29: Katy Perry headlines SoFi Stadium (LA, June 12), Alanis Morissette and Michael Bublé headline BMO Field (Toronto, June 12), with Palestinian-Canadian singer Elyanna among the performers. Canada also confirmed their 26-man squad on May 29 (Alphonso Davies, Jonathan David). Iran beat The Gambia 3-1 in a warm-up in Antalya on May 29, but their ambassador to Mexico held a Tijuana press conference calling out 'the country to the north' — as of May 31, not a single Iranian delegation member has a US visa with 11 days to kickoff. Iran's squad is based at Centro Xoloitzcuintle in Tijuana, set to commute across the border. FIFA's written guarantee that visas will come has no confirmed timeline from the US State Department. The FIFA final squad deadline is June 1; all 48 rosters publish June 2. The USMNT face Senegal in a warm-up at Bank of America Stadium, Charlotte (3:30 PM EDT today).
